questions.question: Name at least three possible hazards that may be encountered during typical ground operations, such as during engine run-up or taxiing?
questions.idealAnswer: The possibility of fire, especially during engine starting. 'fuming props, rotors, prop or jet blast and inlet areas. Other aircraft, vehicles, people and obstacles. Foreign objects such as rocks, gravel, rags, or loose hardware. High noise levels that might cause hearing damage. Hydraulic lock in radial engines. Weathervaning of tailwheel aircraft.

questions.question: What is the most generally used knot for tying down small aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: The bowline (although other anti-slip knots may be used).

questions.question: Describe the precautions that should be taken to protect life and property while starting and running an aircraft engine.
questions.idealAnswer: Study the procedures in the Airplane Flight Manual. Be sure the propeller or inlet area is clear and check for loose stones, gravel, etc. that could be sucked into the prop or engine. Also ensure that the prop or jet blast doesn't blow into hangars or other airplanes, and have a fire guard nearby.

questions.question: If an engine induction fire occurs while starting a reciprocating engine, what procedure should be followed to extinguish the fire?
questions.idealAnswer: Continue cranking the engine to start it and suck the fire into the engine. If the engine doesn't start and the fire continues to burn, discontinue the start attempt and extinguish the fire with a suitable fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What safety procedures must be observed when hand-propping a small aircraft engine?
questions.idealAnswer: Become thoroughly trained. Have a qualified person in the cockpit, check the brakes, call "SWITCH OFF'' before moving the prop, and make sure you have solid footing. When ready to start, call 'CONTACT" and listen for the reply. Swing the prop with the flat of your hand and move back from the prop arc.

questions.question: What procedure should be followed prior to starting a large radial engine to detect and/or prevent a hydraulic lock in the cylinders?
questions.idealAnswer: Pull the propeller through by hand for three or four complete revolutions. Resistance to the prop turning indicates a possible hydraulic lock in at least one of the cylinders.

questions.question: What is the cause of hydraulic lock in large radial engines?
questions.idealAnswer: Oil seeps by the piston rings and accumulates in the combustion chamber of lower cylinders. When a piston comes up on its compression stroke, the incompressible liquid seizes it.

questions.question: What is meant by the term "Hot Start" when starting a jet engine?
questions.idealAnswer: Ignition occurs with an excessively rich mixture, leading to a rapid temperature rise that can exceed the exhaust gas temperature limit.

questions.question: When towing an aircraft, should you use the tow vehicle or aircraft brakes to stop the aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: The tow vehicle brakes should be used except in an emergency - then the aircraft brakes may be used. When towing an aircraft, always apply the tractor brakes for slowing and stopping.

questions.question: Why should an aircraft technician become familiar with standard light signals?
questions.idealAnswer: Light signals may be used when taxiing an airplane without a radio or when a radio becomes inoperative on a tower controlled airport.

questions.question: If a mixture of aviation gasoline and jet fuel is used in a reciprocating aircraft engine, what are the possible results?
questions.idealAnswer: Avgas contaminated by jet fuel must not be used in piston engines - the engine may be damaged or destroyed.

questions.question: What does the number 100 signify in 100LL aviation gasoline?
questions.idealAnswer: It refers to the lean mixture performance number (or octane rating) of the fuel.

questions.question: Is it permissible to use avgas in a turbine engine?
questions.idealAnswer: Limited operation may be allowed by the manufacturer. Continued use may reduce efficiency due to lead deposits on the turbine blades.

questions.question: What are some of the possible outcomes of using a lower grade of avgas than the specified grade?
questions.idealAnswer: An increased chance of engine damage due to detonation, loss of engine power, and an increased probability of overheating.

concepts.label: An increased chance of engine damage due to detonation
terms: an increased chance of engine damage due to detonation

questions.question: Part 23.973 of the FAA regulations specifies that certain markings must be placed adjacent to fuel filler openings. What markings are used for reciprocating engine-powered airplanes?
questions.idealAnswer: The filler openings must be marked with the fuel grade and the word "AVGAS."

questions.question: Describe the important precautions that should be observed when fueling an aircraft.
questions.idealAnswer: Be certain you are using the correct fuel, properly ground the aircraft and refueling unit, and protect the aircraft surfaces from hose and nozzle damage.

questions.question: The marking requirements for oil tank filler openings are specified by FAR 23.1157. What markings are required for a piston engine powered airplane?
questions.idealAnswer: The word "OIL" and the permissible grades and/or types or a reference to the appropriate Airplane Flight Manual for permissible grades and/or types.

questions.question: Where can the standard aircraft taxi hand signals be found?
questions.idealAnswer: In the Aeronautical Information Manual (AIM).

questions.question: Under what conditions should a reciprocating engine be pre-oiled?
questions.idealAnswer: Prior to starting a new engine or one that has been preserved for storage. This ensures adequate lubrication on initial startup.

questions.question: Under what conditions may automobile gasoline be used in an aircraft engine?
questions.idealAnswer: Only if approved by the FAA, usually by the issuance of a Supplemental Type Certificate (STC).

questions.question: What are the indications of water in aircraft fuel after draining a sample from the fuel sumps?
questions.idealAnswer: The sample may have a cloudy or hazy appearance or a solid slug of water.

questions.question: What damage is most likely to occur if excessive force is exerted on the crankshaft when there is liquid lock?
questions.idealAnswer: The force can bend or break a connecting rod or permanently damage the cylinder.

questions.question: Why must aircraft and fuel trucks be grounded together with a grounding cable?
questions.idealAnswer: To eliminate the buildup of static electricity that could result in explosion.

questions.question: Describe the system used to designate performance rating of aviation gasoline.
questions.idealAnswer: For fuels below grade 100, octane numbers are used. For fuels above grade 100, the numbers represent the performance rating of the fuel compared to 100 percent iso—octane.

questions.question: What color is low lead 100 dyed?
questions.idealAnswer: Blue

questions.question: What are the functions of tetraethyl lead in avgas?
questions.idealAnswer: To lubricate and reduce detonation.

questions.question: What is the result of mixing aviation gasoline with jet fuel in a turbine engine?
questions.idealAnswer: When aviation gasoline is mixed with jet fuel, the tetraethyl lead in the gasoline will form deposits on the turbine blades and vanes. Continued use of mixed fuel may cause a loss in engine efficiency. However, there will be no detrimental effect on the engine if such usage is on a limited basis.

questions.question: What are the safety requirements when starting and running a powerplant?
questions.idealAnswer: Use the correct checklist, position the aircraft into the wind, check the prop blast area, secure the external power cart and use a fireguard.

terms: position the aircraft into the wind

questions.question: What are safety precautions when operating a drill press?
questions.idealAnswer: Wear eye and ear protection, clamp the workpiece securely, adjust for the proper RPM, stop machine completely before adjusting workpiece and clean the area when finished.

concepts.label: stop machine completely before adjusting workpiece
terms: stop machine completely before adjusting workpiece

questions.question: Why is a tire cage recommended when inflating aircraft tires?
questions.idealAnswer: To prevent possible personal injury should the tire or wheel fail.

questions.question: What type of fire can a CO2 extinguisher be used on?
questions.idealAnswer: Class A, B, and C type fires.
